chapter: The cancelled dance and race in New Orleans
title: Armstrong's anger over segregation and the mixed band
summary: Louis came back with a mixed band and met resistance from New Orleans laws and attitudes in the mid-1960s.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Uh... But as I understand that he didn't... He didn't come back to New Orleans or did... Didn't he publicly state that he wouldn't come back to New Orleans in his last years or something like that?
No, I didn't... I couldn't say that. No.
Because he was very angry at New Orleans when he died. Not, of course, his people but the city, I think, for the segregationist policies and things like that.

Well, plenty of things. You see, Louis, when Louis came out here, Louis came back with a mixed band. He thought that wasn't... That's what he said. All kind of laws on that. He could play everywhere, but with New Orleans, they didn't want no mixed band. And all that kind of thing. It was very disappointing because he had that kind of chore.
And this was in the 50s or 60s? It was recently.

It almost looked like yesterday, you know? Really? You know how this thing changed. Yeah. I guess it was what? Mid 60s, something like that. Yeah. But Louis, Jack Keek, all of them... Jack Keek, all of them came out here and played with Louis. He was playing the same band. Mm-hmm. Came here with him. But the place he was going, he was going to Texas, he didn't have no trouble. Down here, there was a little... A little... A question of feeling about it, you know? Yeah.
